raw_response:
I’m 50 this year, and I’ve farmed here in Quzhou a long time, so I mostly go by what I’ve seen on my own land and what the people around me are doing. My place is only 7 mu, not big, and with only 2 people in the household and some off-farm work, I can’t spread myself too thin. Cotton takes more watching and more picking labor later on, while spring maize is more straightforward, so this year I’ll keep the land in spring maize. I have a well, so if the weather turns dry I’m not completely stuck, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water unless the field really needs it. For fertilizer, the extension people say one thing and in practice I usually go a bit by the crop look and by past years. Maize can’t go hungry early, so I’ll put most of the fertilizer down at planting and then add some more around the big bell stage if the stand looks good. I’ll use hybrid seed because local saved maize seed is not as reliable for yield. I won’t spend too heavily, because with a small household and outside work, cash on hand matters more than chasing the absolute highest yield.
